prompt:
You are watching a volleyball match from a fixed camera.

This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match.

List ONLY specific meaningful volleyball events in live play.
1. A live rally strictly begins with a 'serve' and ends when the ball is dead. IGNORE all casual touches, practice hits, and dead-ball passing between points.
2. Volleyball rallies follow a logical flow: Serve -> Receive -> Pass -> Attack -> Dig. Use this sequence to classify events accurately. A 'receive' defends a serve; a 'dig' defends an attack.
3. Skip routine intermediate passes. Only report an event if it clearly matches a definition below.

For each event give:
  t       - the precise time the player physically strikes the ball
  type    - must be one of:
            serve: the initial hit from behind the baseline that starts a rally
            receive: the first contact defending a serve
            dig: the first contact defending an attack
            set: an assist pass that directly leads to a kill
            attack: an offensive hit sent over the net that does not score a point
            kill: an attack that directly scores a point and ends the rally
            block: deflecting an attack at the net
  side    - "left" or "right": which side of the net the player is on (left half or right half of the screen)
  number  - the player's jersey number as a string, or null if you cannot read it
  error   - true if the touch was a mistake
  point   - true if the rally ended here and a point was scored
